# Handle an employee grievance

[Overview](#overview) · [Before you start](#before-you-start) · [Steps](#steps-at-a-glance)

## Overview

When a worker raises a workplace concern outside the immediate safety or harassment-response route. A confidential documented outcome with an impartial review route and tracked corrective actions.

Start with the applicability facts and evidence listed in the first step. Resolve missing facts before authorizing the affected work. Completion requires the documented outcome, including tracked exceptions; starting an application or recording a task is not evidence of completion.

> This is an operational coordination guide. Confirm the applicable company facts, contracts and jurisdictions before acting. Qualified advisers own legal, tax, safety or regulatory determinations and any required professional work. The cited authorities describe their named jurisdictions or frameworks; their rules are not asserted for other countries. External actions require approval for the specific action.

> Editorial status: operational draft. Source pages checked on 2026-10-29. No case-specific legal review, professional assurance or completed execution is claimed.

## Step details

<a id="step-1"></a>

### 1. Record the concern and preserve relevant evidence

agent-runnable


Capture the employee's account, requested outcome and any immediate safety or retaliation concerns. Restrict access and route urgent safety, harassment or criminal concerns to the appropriate specialist response.

- Sources: [Acas disciplinary and grievance procedures](https://www.acas.org.uk/acas-code-of-practice-on-disciplinary-and-grievance-procedures/html)

<a id="step-2"></a>

### 2. Choose an impartial and applicable process

human · human approval required


HR or the designated reviewer confirms conflicts, local requirements, representation and policy steps. Explain who will handle the concern and distinguish an informal discussion from a formal investigation.

- Sources: [Acas disciplinary and grievance procedures](https://www.acas.org.uk/acas-code-of-practice-on-disciplinary-and-grievance-procedures/html)

<a id="step-3"></a>

### 3. Hear the parties and investigate the facts

human · human approval required


The appointed reviewer gathers relevant accounts and documents fairly, giving people an appropriate opportunity to respond. Protect confidentiality without promising secrecy that prevents a proper review.

- Sources: [Acas disciplinary and grievance procedures](https://www.acas.org.uk/acas-code-of-practice-on-disciplinary-and-grievance-procedures/html)

<a id="step-4"></a>

### 4. Review and communicate the decision

human · human approval required


The authorized decision maker evaluates findings, proposed remedies and employment-law advice. Communicate the approved outcome and applicable review or appeal route, limiting disclosure of other people's personal information.

- Sources: [Acas disciplinary and grievance procedures](https://www.acas.org.uk/acas-code-of-practice-on-disciplinary-and-grievance-procedures/html)

<a id="step-5"></a>

### 5. Track remedies and protect against recurrence

agent-runnable


Record action owners, dates and follow-up with the affected employee. Check for retaliation and recurring issues and retain the case evidence under the approved retention and access rules.

- Verify: A confidential documented outcome with an impartial review route and tracked corrective actions.
- Sources: [Acas disciplinary and grievance procedures](https://www.acas.org.uk/acas-code-of-practice-on-disciplinary-and-grievance-procedures/html)
